official_measurement_examples.name: Main River definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: The statutory map defines watercourses designated as Main Rivers in England; designation gives the Environment Agency regulatory powers but not a duty to maintain every mapped reach.

official_measurement_examples.name: Variation status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 6 July 2026 variations dataset contains proposed changes and must not be treated as already-designated Main River geometry.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ordinary watercourse distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Open watercourses not designated as Main River are generally ordinary watercourses regulated through LLFA or IDB consent routes.

official_measurement_examples.name: 8 metre trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning guidance says a flood risk activity permit may be required within 8 metres of a non-tidal main river bank, defence or culvert.

official_measurement_examples.name: 16 metre tidal trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: A permit may be required within 16 metres of tidal main-river banks, defences or culverts.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permit separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A flood risk activity permit is distinct from planning permission and ordinary watercourse consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Floodplain activity
official_measurement_examples.fact: Some activities in a main-river floodplain can require a permit where they could affect flood flow or storage and are not controlled by planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Geometry limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A mapped river centreline does not establish parcel access rights, ownership or precise bank-top setback without site evidence.

core_rules: Main River mapping is designation evidence not planning permission
proposed map variations are not current designation
ordinary watercourse and Main River consent routes must not be merged
8 metre permit trigger is not a universal development exclusion zone
16 metre tidal trigger is not a universal development exclusion zone
flood risk activity permit is not planning permission
planning permission is not automatically a flood risk activity permit
map centreline does not prove bank-top location
Environment Agency permissive powers are not a maintenance duty
river geometry does not determine land ownership
permit status does not reserve development capacity
historic river geometry must retain version date
LLFA or IDB consent is distinct from Environment Agency permit
floodplain screening does not replace FRA evidence
no parcel river clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
